title: Variation and evolution
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mutation
items.clue: A change in the DNA of an organism.

items.label: Variation
items.clue: Differences in the characteristics of individuals in a population.

items.label: Evolution
items.clue: A change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time through a process of natural selection, which may result in the formation of a new species.

questions.stem: Two plants grown from cuttings of the same parent plant are given different amounts of light. One grows much taller than the other. What does this difference show?

options.text: The plants inherited different genes for their height
The change in light has caused a mutation in one plant
The environment has influenced the phenotype of the plants
One plant has evolved to be taller in the brighter light

questions.explanation: The genome and its interaction with the environment influence the development of the phenotype, so the different light conditions have produced different heights.

options.text: A change in the characteristics of an animal in its lifetime
A change in the inherited characteristics of a population
A change in appearance that makes a population a new species
The growth of the characteristics that organisms need most

questions.explanation: Evolution is a change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time through a process of natural selection.

questions.stem: Which of these describes the causes of variation between individuals in a population?

options.text: Inherited genes, the conditions of development, or both
Inherited genes alone, which are passed on by the parents
Mutations that are produced by a change in the environment
Mutations alone, because every one changes the phenotype

questions.explanation: Variation may be due to the genes they have inherited, the conditions in which they have developed, or a combination of genes and the environment.

questions.stem: In a beetle population most beetles are pale and a few are dark. The tree bark the beetles live on becomes darker, so birds find the pale beetles more easily. After many generations most of the beetles are dark. Which statement explains this?

options.text: The beetles developed a dark colour because they needed it
Each pale beetle became darker as the tree bark got darker
The darker bark caused the mutations that made beetles darker
Dark beetles survived to breed and passed on their variant

questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on variants that give rise to phenotypes best suited to their environment, and those beetles pass the genes on to the next generation.

questions.stem: All variants arise from mutations. Which statement about mutations and phenotype is correct?

options.text: Most mutations lead to a change in the phenotype
Most mutations have no effect on the phenotype
Mutations happen only when the environment changes
Mutations build up in an organism during its life

questions.explanation: Most variants have no effect on the phenotype, some influence phenotype and very few determine phenotype.

questions.stem: Two populations of one species have been separated for a very long time and now look very different. What must be shown before they are classed as two new species?

options.text: That their phenotypes are different enough to tell apart
That each population has developed the features that it needs
That the individuals have changed during their own lifetimes
That they can no longer produce fertile offspring together

questions.explanation: Two new species have formed when the populations are so different in phenotype that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

questions.stem: A mutation produces a new phenotype in a population. The environment then changes, and the new phenotype is suited to the new conditions. What is the likely result?

options.text: More mutations of the same type occur in the population
A relatively rapid change in the species can take place
Each organism changes to the new phenotype in its lifetime
The organisms develop the new phenotype that they need

questions.explanation: If the new phenotype is suited to an environmental change it can lead to a relatively rapid change in the species.
